title: Ogoma's lemma: realizing an annihilator equality over the localization by multiplying with an element of S

core_obligations: Set K = Ker(pi: M -> M), K' = {m in M : pi^2 m = 0 in S^{-1}M} and Q = K'/K; the hypothesis says S^{-1}Q = 0.
Q is a finite A-module since A is Noetherian, so some s in S annihilates Q.
For this s, Ker(s^n pi) = Ker((s^n pi)^2) for every n > 0: any m killed by (s^n pi)^2 has s^n-pi-torsion image in Q, which s^n annihilates.
proof_roadmap: Torsion quotient construction; finiteness and annihilation; verification of the annihilator equality.
difficulty_reason: A short complete construction; the one substantive step (the torsion quotient annihilator) is written out.
